entities.summary: Émile Noël was a senior French European Union official who played a crucial role in shaping the European integration process from the 1950s to the 1990s. Born in Istanbul in 1922, Noël's early life was marked by his experiences as a refugee during World War II. He joined the French Foreign Ministry in the 1950s and quickly rose through the ranks, becoming a key figure in the development of the European Economic Community (EEC). Noël's diplomatic expertise and commitment to European integration earned him the respect of his peers and the gratitude of European leaders. As the EEC evolved into the European Union, Noël continued to play a leading role, contributing to the creation of the single market and the establishment of the euro. Noël's legacy extends beyond his professional achievements, as he was also a devoted public servant who dedicated his life to the service of others. In his later years, Noël reflected on the importance of European integration, stating, 'The European Union is not a mere economic entity, but a political community that promotes peace, stability, and prosperity.'
